title: The Pantheon
objective: After this level you can describe the Pantheon and its record-breaking dome.
summary: Hadrian’s Pantheon has the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world, lit only by its oculus. As a church it survived intact.

cards.headline: The largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world was built by the Romans.
cards.body: Remember the volcanic concrete from Level 73? This is what it could do at full stretch.

cards.headline: A ball inside a building
cards.body: Pantheon means “of all the gods.” The building standing today is Hadrian’s rebuilding of Agrippa’s first Pantheon. Its dome, about 43 m across, is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world. And the proportions are perfect: the height from the floor to the top of the dome equals its diameter. So a complete sphere 43 m wide would fit inside, resting on the floor.

cards.headline: Light and lightness
cards.body: Look up and there’s a hole in the roof. The oculus, about 8 m wide, is the building’s only source of natural light. The dome itself slims down as it rises: it gets thinner toward the top, and lighter stone was mixed into the concrete higher up. Less weight up high means less weight pressing down on everything below.
cards.callout: Oculus: the open “eye” at the top

cards.fact: The Pantheon survived by changing religion.
cards.context: In 609 CE the temple “of all the gods” became a Christian church, which helped it survive intact. New job, same building.
